answer:
For every m≥7,
\[|K_m|\simeq \bigvee^{q-r}S^{m-3}\ \vee\ \bigvee^{p-r}S^{m-2}\ \vee\ \bigvee_{\substack{1\le a\le r\\d_a>1}}M(\mathbb Z/d_a\mathbb Z,m-3),\]
where the following finite arithmetic formulas specify all the multiplicities and cyclic orders.

Put p=∑_{s=0}^4 2^s binom(m,s), q=3(binom(m,4)+(m−2)binom(m,3)), and h=min(p,q). Index p columns by (S,α), where S⊆[m], |S|≤4, and α:S→{1,2}. For |A|=4 and c:A→{1,2,3}, define
\[L_{S,\alpha}(A,c)=\begin{cases}(-1)^{|\{j\in S:c(j)=3\}|},&S\subseteq A,\ c(j)=3\ (j\in A\setminus S),\ c(j)\in\{\alpha(j),3\}\ (j\in S),\\0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\]
Define a q×p integer array b by including, for each i∈{1,2,3}, these rows:
• for each A∈binom([m],4), the row with entries L_{S,α}(A,i^A);
• for each T∈binom([m],3), putting j_T=min([m]∖T), the row with entries ∑_{a=1}^3 L_{S,α}(T∪{j_T},i^T∪{j_T↦a});
• for each T∈binom([m],3) and j∉T, putting a_i=min({1,2,3}∖{i}), the row with entries L_{S,α}(T∪{j},i^T∪{j↦a_i}).

Set Δ₀=1 and, for 1≤a≤h,
\[\Delta_a=\gcd_{\substack{1\le u_1<\cdots<u_a\le q\\1\le v_1<\cdots<v_a\le p}}\left|\sum_{\pi\in\mathfrak S_a}\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)\prod_{\ell=1}^a b_{u_\ell,v_{\pi(\ell)}}\right|,\]
with the gcd of an all-zero family defined to be zero. Set r=∑_{a=1}^h ε(Δ_a), where ε(0)=0 and ε(x)=1 for x>0, and set d_a=Δ_a/Δ_{a−1} for 1≤a≤r. Repeated values d_a>1 give repeated Moore-space summands; a wedge with zero summands is a point.
